finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF and arbitrary file read. The POST parameter `feed` is passed directly to file_get_contents() with no scheme, host or IP validation. An attacker can make the server fetch internal URLs (http://169.254.169.254/, localhost services, internal hosts), use other wrappers (file://, php://, ftp://, and so on), and read local files. Only the response length is echoed, which limits direct exfiltration. It still works as a blind oracle for port and host scanning and for response sizes, and it can trigger side effects on internal services.

trace.note: Only checks that the request is a POST and that `feed` is set. No authentication.
Attacker-controlled value goes straight into file_get_contents(), which follows URL wrappers.
strlen of the fetched body is echoed back, giving an oracle for response size and reachability.

finding.guards_checked: No require_admin() call on this path. No scheme allowlist, host allowlist, private-IP blocklist or DNS-rebinding protection. No use of parse_url or filter_var.

verdict.reason: import.php:11-13 passes $_POST['feed'] straight to file_get_contents() and echoes strlen() with no auth (require_admin is defined at line 4 but only called at line 18 for a different branch) and no scheme/host validation, and import.php is the only file in the directory.

finding.claim: Admin-gated SSRF. The `set_webhook` POST parameter is passed to curl_init() and executed with curl_exec() with no URL validation. A user with the admin session flag can make the server request arbitrary internal URLs, including cloud metadata endpoints. CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER is set but the body is discarded, so this is blind SSRF. Severity is lower because it requires admin privileges, but the missing validation would still let a compromised or malicious admin reach internal services. The curl default also permits redirects only if CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION is set, and it is not set here. Other curl protocols (gopher://, file://) are not restricted, since CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS is not set.
finding.source: $_POST['set_webhook'] (HTTP POST body, requires an admin session)
finding.sink: curl_init($hook) followed by curl_exec($ch) at import.php:20-22

trace.note: Entry point: `set_webhook` is present in the POST data.
The value is assigned to $hook with no sanitization.
curl_exec() sends the request to the attacker-chosen URL.

finding.guards_checked: require_admin() restricts this to admin sessions. There is no URL scheme or host allowlist, no private-IP blocklist, and no CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS restriction. CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION is not enabled.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin() at import.php:4-9 and :18 (session is_admin check). It is an auth gate, not a URL validator. No URL validation exists.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code (import.php:17-22), but the sink at import.php:20 is reached only after require_admin() at import.php:18, and nothing in the directory ever sets $_SESSION['is_admin'], so an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker cannot control the value.
